text:
Maya S.: FYI: coordinated docs + SDK change scheduled tomorrow 02:00 UTC. We're renaming the request parameter from `request_stream` to `response_mode`. This affects generated client examples and quickstarts.

Tim R.: Are we doing a deprecation window or immediate break?

Maya S.: 30-day deprecation window. Hosted API will accept the old key and return an `X-Redwood-Deprecation: response_mode` header plus a warning in the response body. After 30 days the old key will be rejected with 400.

Olga P.: Can SDKs include a compatibility shim so users don't immediately break?

Samir K.: Yes. Draft shims in PRs: js-sdk PR (accept both keys, console.warn) and py-sdk PR (warn via logging). Tests added. I'll paste links in the Confluence doc.

Maya S.: Rollout plan: 1) publish migration guide + codemod examples today, 2) publish docs site + enable support banner at 02:00 UTC tomorrow, 3) hard reject old param after 30 days.

Quick codemod (POSIX sed):
```
find docs -name "*.md" -exec sed -i 's/request_stream/response_mode/g' {} +
```

Tim R.: We should notify customers. Draft email on Confluence, support playbook attached.

Olga P.: In the release notes call out exact sample changes and advise platform teams to pin client versions during the window.

Samir K.: I'll add an automated codemod job in js-sdk CI and merge compatibility shims before docs publish. Target merge ~1855554500.

docs-bot: Docs build queued; search reindex scheduled for 2026-03-29 02:00 UTC. Redirects for old examples in place.

Maya S.: Thanks — I'll post a short announcement in #general and ping Sales/CS once live.

Tim R.: Thanks all.

Olga P.: LGTM, will monitor support channel during rollout.

Samir K.: Follow-up will include PR links and a one-paragraph changelog blurb for the announcement.
